title: What the Python SDK does with a response: key casing, models, the response object

prose.text: Python SDK methods return `(result, response, error)`; the result is built from a response body whose keys the SDK has already rewritten.

prose.label: Key casing.
prose.text: {{response-keys-camel-cased}} Where a product's models then look up snake_case keys, the multi-word fields come back empty: [[zcc.sdk-python.wire-keys:response-keys-camel-cased]], [[zidentity.sdk-python:form-response-camel]], [[zdx.sdk-python.response-models:multiword-attrs-lost]].

prose.label: Models.
prose.text: {{as-dict}} Result models subclass the SDK's object base class: [[zpa.sdk-python.return-shapes:result-models-subclass]].

response-keys-camel-cased.statement: `form_response_body` camel-cases every key of a response body, recursing into nested objects and into objects inside lists, and leaves out keys whose value is None.

as-dict.statement: A model's as_dict returns snake_case keys and omits attributes whose value is None, while its request_format method is the camelCase form the API expects.

quotes: # Otherwise it's a simple type (string, int, etc.) else: result[to_snake_case(key)] = val
The keys are in camelCase as expected by the API.

status-accessor.statement: `ZscalerAPIResponse` keeps the HTTP status in `_status`, reads it from the underlying response once in its constructor, and exposes it through `get_status()`.

quotes: self._status = res_details.status_code if res_details and hasattr(res_details, "status_code") else None

no-status-code-attr.statement: `ZscalerAPIResponse` defines no `status_code` attribute or property of its own, so callers read the status through `get_status()`.
no-status-code-attr.conditions: An absence: a search of zscaler/oneapi_response.py at the pin finds status_code only in the constructor line that reads res_details.status_code into _status.

search-current-page.statement: The response object's search method applies a JMESPath expression to the current page of results only, so filtering across a collection means searching each page.

quotes: `.search()` operates on the current page. To filter across all pages, apply it to each page as you paginate:
The `.search()` method applies a JMESPath expression to the current page of results and returns a list of matching items.

tuple-return.statement: Python SDK methods return a three-element tuple of result, response and error rather than a bare result.

checks.do: Whether a None model attribute is really absent from the response, or a multi-word key the model looked up under its snake_case name after the response was camel-cased.
